subject.title: Feature: configurable mediaLocalRoots for image tool

question: Should OpenClaw support broad host-local media reads through a shared tools.fs.roots-style policy, a narrower media-only root allowlist, or no persistent host-root expansion?
rationale: The choice changes what host filesystem paths model-facing tools may read, and repository policy treats new config/default surfaces and filesystem boundaries as maintainer/security decisions.

options.title: Use shared filesystem roots
options.body: Adopt one reviewed tools.fs.roots-style contract for filesystem tools and media paths so OpenClaw avoids competing allowlists.

options.title: Add media-only roots
options.body: Expose a narrower media root field if maintainers want image/PDF/media reads decoupled from read/write/edit filesystem policy, with explicit docs and tests for the split boundary.

options.title: Keep current boundary
options.body: Continue requiring managed inbound media, channel-scoped attachment roots, workspace copies, or symlinks instead of persistent host-root expansion.

recommendation.title: Use shared filesystem roots
recommendation.body: Adopt one reviewed tools.fs.roots-style contract for filesystem tools and media paths so OpenClaw avoids competing allowlists.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged local-root policy work is closest to the current configuration-derived media-root boundary.
